tldr: Training-free recursive self-improvement for brand-new computer environments: curriculum, actor, and verifier agents explore with a broad-then-deep strategy and consolidate verified experience into a memory that is frozen for test-time reuse — lifting open models (GLM-5.3 + Kimi-K3) past GPT-6 Astra on OSWorld 2.0 and Agents' Last Exam.
method: One durable, evolvable memory driven by three coordinated roles: a curriculum agent generates practice tasks from knowledge gaps and decides when practice stops; actor agents execute them code-as-policy and distill their own verified experience back into memory; a verifier agent judges outcomes from environment evidence alone, isolated from the actor's private reasoning to reduce correlated errors. Exploration is broad-then-deep — Broad Recursive Self-exploration (BRS) runs parallel task waves from a shared memory snapshot, consolidated serially per wave with budgets checked at wave boundaries; Deep Recursive Self-exploration (DRS) then does sequential, progressively harder targeted practice, each verified experience committed before the next task is proposed. At test time the memory is frozen and the curriculum agent and memory updates are disabled.
results: OSWorld 2.0 (0808 offline, 82 tasks): partial score 71.97 -> 78.98 and binary accuracy 37.80 -> 42.68 with the same harness and frozen models — above GPT-6 Astra (72.60) and Claude Opus 5 (70.19).

Agents' Last Exam Near-term (67 tasks): 83.75 -> 84.82 partial and 49.25 -> 50.75 binary — partial above GPT-6 Astra (82.26), though binary stays below Astra's 52.24 (the paper's own Appendix C.4 notes the partial-credit advantage does not extend to every metric).

Stage ablation on four OSWorld tasks: full broad+deep 74.54 mean vs 65.52 broad-only and 56.50 deep-only; deep-only from empty memory falls below the baseline on two tasks, so starting focused can hurt.

GameCraft-Bench (40 tasks): improves game quality from both weak and strong base generators, where the Play2Code baseline degrades already-strong games; RSI experience adds further gain on every generator.
advantages: A pure memory artifact, not weights: model parameters are fixed through exploration and evaluation, yet the same actor-verifier harness goes 71.97 -> 78.98 partial and 37.80 -> 42.68 binary on OSWorld 2.0 (0808 offline, 82 tasks) — clearing GPT-6 Astra (72.60) by 6.38 points and Claude Opus 5 (70.19), and showing agent-level self-improvement can reverse the open- vs closed-source gap without training.

A concrete concurrency/consistency protocol for parallel memory building that prior memory-based self-improvement leaves underspecified: every project in a BRS wave starts from the same immutable pre-wave memory snapshot and cannot observe sibling work or outcomes; after all verdicts land, the same actor contexts resume one at a time in curriculum-authored order, each distilling and reconciling into the latest canonical memory; the nominal eight-project budget is checked only at completed wave boundaries (four concurrent, so realized project count can exceed eight) and the next wave is chosen only after those commits finish.

Verification isolation as an explicit information boundary, not just a second prompt: the verifier derives checks from the authoritative task and the candidate environment with the actor's memory, private reasoning, and execution logs hidden, inspects a QEMU checkpoint that the harness restores before grading (so verifier probes cannot alter the scored artifact), and may return UNVERIFIED rather than forcing a verdict; only completed actor learning updates are promoted to canonical memory, while the curriculum agent edits only a disposable copy it never syncs back.

Empirical support for broad-then-deep ordering, including the counterexample: full RSI averages 74.54 partial on four OSWorld tasks versus 65.52 broad-only and 56.50 deep-only, and deep-only from empty memory falls below the no-exploration baseline on T085 and T089 — targeted hard-case practice without prior broad coverage can actively hurt, while broad-only improves over baseline on every task.
limitations: The headline RSI column is not a matched re-run: only 41/82 OSWorld tasks (19/67 ALE) have recorded RSI entries, baseline scores are retained for the rest, and selected retries/checkpoints with differing budgets are included — the repo's PAPER.md documents this aggregation scope.

The acceptance signal is an LLM verifier reading environment evidence, not executed tests; the paper's own failure analysis finds verifier PASS without full requirement coverage and incorrect rules persisting in memory — the failure class rsif moves behind programmatic held-out gates.
Per-environment exploration is expensive (Linux host, Docker/KVM VMs, nominal eight BRS projects per target); gains are demonstrated on two computer-use benchmarks plus one game-development setting.
fits: The closest large-scale cousin of rsif's design: weights frozen, a single artifact (memory) evolves under a trusted outer protocol, verification is separated from acting and isolated from the actor's reasoning, and the result is frozen before evaluation. rsif generalizes the evolving surface (prompt/skill/module/memory/policy/meta), replaces the LLM verifier with executed held-out gates plus canaries, and adds archive/promotion/rollback; RSIAgent shows the pattern surviving at full computer-use scale with open models. Its curriculum actor also mirrors rsif's improver-as-proposal-generator split.
reading: Read Sections 3.2-3.3 for the role split and broad/deep staging, then Section 4.6's failure-mode taxonomy (untargeted exploration, incomplete verification, unreliable memory consolidation) as a checklist for any RSI loop; the repo's docs/ARCHITECTURE.md maps paper stages onto runnable phases (BRS/DRS/test-time reuse).
